News.title: ‘Killer’ nurse Lucy Letby saved my baby’s life twice – the jury in her trial was misled, says dad
News.content:
A DAD whose baby’s life was saved twice by Lucy Letby believes the jury in her trial were misled.

Carl Bolton’s daughter Jessica was born at the Countess of Chester Hospital via cesarean section at 36 weeks and was taken onto the neonatal unit due to her difficulty breathing.





There she was cared for by Letby, who would later be convicted of the murder of seven premature babies, and the attempted murder of seven more.

However, Carl says on what was a chaotic unit she was “about the only one in there who seemed to really know what she was doing”.

And later he would learn Letby “went above and beyond” to save Jessica’s life, with the tot – who was a transverse lie – being the “sickest baby on the unit for 24 hours”.

He said he believes the chaotic condition and state of the unit “wasn’t really a factor” in Letby’s conviction – and therefore the jury could have been misled by not being given the full facts.



He claims he and wife Jessica had no idea how ill their daughter was at the time, and is still waiting for full answers from the hospital trust.

Speaking on Good Morning Britain today, the dad said: “She (Letby) was the only one who really explained anything to us and really gave us the time to tell us what had happened to Jessica.



“The whole unit was very busy, everyone was rushing around everywhere but Lucy took the time to explain to us the procedures that had taken place, and that she was doing fine.”

Asked if he ever felt his baby was at risk around Letby, he answered “no”, before describing a moment in which other nurses treating an infant next to them said “we don’t understand why this baby keeps stopping breathing”.

Carl said: “That was terrifying for us.”



He said during the five days they were at the hospital, they never spoke to a doctor, and described the unit as an environment where “it wouldn’t take much more for it to blow up like a bottle of pop”.

Asked if he believes Letby saved his baby’s life, Carl said: “I don’t believe that, that’s what we’ve been told by the hospital and the police.”

He said on two separate occasions Jessica needed to be intubated and was given surfactant into her lungs, a medical procedure normally only for premature babies.

The charges Letby has been convicted of in full Child A, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby injected air intravenously into the bloodstream of the baby boy. COUNT 1 GUILTY. Child B, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby attempted to murder the baby girl, the twin sister of Child A, by injecting air into her bloodstream. COUNT 2 GUILTY. Child C, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said Letby forced air down a feeding tube and into the stomach of the baby boy. COUNT 3 GUILTY. Child D, allegation of murder. The Crown said air was injected intravenously into the baby girl. COUNT 4 GUILTY. Child E, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby murdered the twin baby boy with an injection of air into the bloodstream and also deliberately caused bleeding to the infant. COUNT 5 GUILTY. Child F, allegation of attempted murder. Letby was said by prosecutors to have poisoned the twin brother of Child E with insulin. COUNT 6 GUILTY. Child I, allegation of murder. The prosecution said Letby killed the baby girl at the fourth attempt and had given her air and overfed her with milk. COUNT 12 GUILTY. Child K, allegation of attempted murder. The prosecution said Letby compromised the baby girl as she deliberately dislodged a breathing tube. COUNT 14 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT AT ORIGINAL TRIAL, NOW GUILTY AFTER RETRIAL Child L, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said the nurse poisoned the twin baby boy with insulin. COUNT 15 GUILTY. Child M, allegation of attempted murder. Prosecutors said Letby injected air into the bloodstream of Child L’s twin brother. COUNT 16 GUILTY. Child N, three allegations of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby inflicted trauma in the baby boy’s throat and also injected him with air in the bloodstream. COUNT 17 GUILTY, COUNT 18 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT, COUNT 19 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT. Child O, allegation of murder. Prosecutors say Letby attacked the triplet boy by injecting him with air, overfeeding him with milk and inflicting trauma to his liver with “severe force”. COUNT 20 GUILTY. Child P, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said the nurse targeted the triplet brother of Child O by overfeeding him with milk, injecting air and dislodging his breathing tube. COUNT 21 GUILTY. Child Q, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby injected the baby boy with liquid, and possibly air, down his feeding tube. COUNT 22 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT

And there were two other examples of “pale moments”, which in hindsight could probably be attributed to acid reflux.

He claims he and Claire were not kept informed about exactly what was happening and how serious Jessica’s condition was.



Three years later, when they finally sat down for a meeting with the hospital trust, he said the extent of Letby’s involvement was given in more detail.

Carl said: “The words that the gentleman used were ‘she escalated her care and on the second occasion she went above and beyond her call of duty’.

“Those were the words he used, what he meant by that I don’t know – I don’t know what exactly she did do.”

When Carl and wife Claire heard Letby had been arrested in July 2018, he approached the police to see if Jessica could form part of the investigation.

“The police said on three occasions, your daughter is not involved in the investigation, we’ve ruled her out,” he said.



Carl went on to say, Letby’s actions to save his daughter does not mean she is innocent of harming other infants.

However, he said: “We feel that the process was unfair.

“We feel the jury wasn’t given the full information about that unit.”

Carl said he and Claire came to that conclusion after watching a documentary about Letby’s case.

“It was obvious from that documentary that the condition and state of that unit wasn’t really a factor in the conviction,” he said.



“For me and Claire, that just didn’t make any sense. It seems like they’ve reached an extraordinary explanation for something that could be explained by a failing unit.”

He added that the couple were only told the full extent of Jessica’s condition on the unit at the meeting three years later.

The hospital itself has since “been very closed” and it’s been “very difficult” to get answers “out of anybody”.

“Until three years later when we sat down with the hospital we had no idea how poorly Jessica was,” Carl explained.

“In fact, we’d thought she’d done reasonably well. It turned out she was the sickest baby on the unit for 24 hours.”



He added: “The real story here is how we’ve been ignored and dismissed and left to our own devices by the hospital, and Claire suffered for 10 years because of that, mentally.”

Letby is serving 15 whole-life orders, following two trials in 2023 and 2024.

However, since her sentencing, there’s been growing feeling amongst many experts that her convictions were “unsafe”, and she could have been the victim of a miscarriage of justice.

Her legal team, headed by barrister Mark McDonald, has submitted an application to the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC), which could see Letby’s case referred back to the Court of Appeal and her convictions quashed.

The Sun has approached the Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust for comment.

News.title: Moment feral thug slashes her love rival’s face with wine glass in nightclub attack that almost blinded victim
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a female thug slashed a love rival’s face with a wine glass in a nightclub attack.

Jade Hill, 21, almost blinded victim Georgina Kilburn, who is in a relationship with the yob’s ex.





Hill also lashed out at one of Georgina’s friends when she stepped in to help.

Georgina was left covered in blood and needed more than 20 stitches for three deep gashes on the side of her face.

Her pal also needed hospital treatment following the savage attack at The Closet in Weymouth, Dorset, on October 12, 2024.

Hill has now been jailed for four years after she was found guilty of causing the two women grievous bodily harm with intent.

The court heard Hill made a bee-line for love rival Georgina after seeing her in the club.

She hurled abuse at the victim before smashing the wine glass in her face – sending shards flying into the air.



A pal then grabbed Hill in a bid to restrain her but the thug struck her with the broken wine glass.

The nightclub DJ can be heard interrupting the song of Sex on Fire by Kings of Leon to call for door staff to help.

Hill was arrested at the scene by police while her two victims went to hospital.



Georgina, who has been left with permanent scarring, described Hill’s behaviour as vile and accused her of making up lies.

She said: “Jade has not once accepted her actions, apologised to me or shown any remorse. She does not care about what she has done and is only sorry now that she is in prison.

“It was not a split second decision. The judge referenced to how I’m minding my own business and her friend has to try and pull her away from literally coming at me with a glass.

“She then decided to brush him off and continue to come at me holding the stem of the wine glass and swinging it very high above her head and smashing directly into my face.

“My friend then intervened to help me and she then hit the brunt of the wine glass into her head two times and then she proceeded to run out and tell security and police that she was the one attacked.



“There is no excuse for such vile behaviour and I deserve the justice that has been served, I do not deserve threatening messages or people claiming I’m lying.”

Detective Constable Holly Hetherington, of Dorset CID, said the attack was “violent and unprovoked”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added: “Officers responded quickly to arrest the defendant and we have worked to compile evidence to hold her to account for her offending.

“I want to thank the victims and witnesses who gave evidence at trial and helped to bring Hill to justice.”

News.title: Ex-beauty queen, 30, punched boyfriend in face in row & falsely branded him ‘paedo’ after date night in pub
News.content:
DINNER ROW Ex-beauty queen, 30, punched boyfriend in face in row & falsely branded him ‘paedo’ after date night in pub

A FORMER beauty queen beat up her boyfriend and falsely branded him a paedophile after they rowed during a date night.

Anna Brumskill, 30, had been out for a meal and a drink with Kevin Willis at a gastro pub in Rainhill on Merseyside – but the pair began arguing soon after they left to go home.





Mr Willis was phoning her mother when Brumskill – who won Miss Teen Galaxy and reached the finals of Miss Teen England and Miss Teen Great Britain when she was a schoolgirl – struck him in the face and grabbed the phone.

She later bombarded him with menacing phone calls and messages threatening to “smash the place up” and calling garage worker Mr Willis a “nonce.”

When charged, Brumskill issued a basis of plea statement saying: ”I accept I made unlawful contact with Kevin Willis but I did so when trying to take the phone off him as he was calling my mother.

”I did not intentionally punch him although I accept a reckless assault when I made contact with his hand or face.”

She also claimed Mr Willis had since tried to make contact with her – and even arranged for her favourite takeaway meal to be delivered to her front door.

The reasons for their argument are not known.



At Sefton magistrates court, Brumskill of Prescot, near Liverpool, admitted stalking and assault by beating.

She was sentenced to a 12-month community order with a requirement she participate in six months of alcohol treatment and complete 25 days of rehabilitative activity.

She was also issued with a six-month restraining order banning her from contacting Mr Willis, although she will be allowed to pass by his home so she can access her local post office to cash her Universal Credit handouts.

Earlier Ed Handley, prosecuting, said: “Kevin Willis details being in a relationship with the defendant for approximately ten months.

“On April 6, they went out for a meal and drink at the Ship Inn but as they started walking down Warrington Road there was a verbal argument.



“He was on the phone to the defendant’s mother and at that point she tried to grab the phone off him. He does detail being contacted on his face causing no injury.

”He then details following police intervention and her being released from custody, she started to harass him by phone calls and emails.

“He said he did reply to one as he was worried about her as she suffers with mental health and he did not want any harm to come to her.”

The barrister told the court that Mr Willis told Brumskill to leave him alone and seek help. He instead received calls and voicemails from a no-caller ID.

He said: “One was threatening to smash the place up. During the course of contact she called him a nonce and a paedophile.”



Brumskill had a previous conviction for resisting police. Her lawyer Philip Lee said: ”She has very limited recollection of the messages that were sent but accepts that they were unpleasant.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It appears she got drunk and made numerous attempts to contact him.

“She certainly regrets that behaviour and ultimately she is sorry for any distress caused to the complainant.”

News.title: Hero schoolboy, 13, desperately tried to save teen pal after he fell in river but both tragically drowned
News.content:
DOUBLE TRAGEDY Hero schoolboy, 13, desperately tried to save teen pal after he fell in river but both tragically drowned

TWO teenage boys tragically drowned in a river after a hero schoolboy jumped into the water to rescue his pal, an inquest heard.

Aras Rudzianskas, 13, was attempting to save David Radut, 14, from the River Tyne in Ovingham, Northumberland, when tragedy struck.





The teenagers had been taking turns playing on a rope swing over the water on May 18, 2024, Northumberland Coroner’s Court heard.

But David, who was unable to swim, let go of the rope over the river on his second attempt – sending him plunging into deep water.

He then shouted to his group of 20 friends on the river bank for help, prompting heroic Aras to jump in after him.

However, amid the panic, the 13-year-old was repeatedly pulled under the water by his desperate pal.

One of the group attempted to grab David, but let go of his arms after they too started being pulled under, Assistant Coroner Paul Dunn said.

But the youngster was not sure whether the pull came from the current in the river or David.

The 14-year-old was never seen by his friends again after vanishing under the water.

Some 36 police officers were scrambled to the river after receiving reports of the incident just before 3.30pm.



Aras’ lifeless body was pulled from the water by paddleboarder Fiona Matthews, who initially thought he was a “pale rock”.

She was made aware of the tragedy after some boys – believed to be pals of David and Aras – asked if she had seen anyone in the water.

Fiona, who then attempted to resuscitate the teen, described the current as less calm than usual on the day of the tragedy.



She told the court: “I pulled him under the arms and used his shorts to try and get him out of the water. I think the adrenaline kicked in.

“I had lost my paddle by then so I was using my hands to paddle.”

Thanks to Fiona’s actions, paramedics were then able to take over and get Aras’ heart beating again.

The teen was then immediately rushed to the Royal Victoria Infirmary by air ambulance.

But despite the best efforts of medical teams, Aras tragically died in the hospital in Newcastle, Tyne and Wear, three days later.



Divers from Northumbria Police confirmed David was discovered hours later after a lengthy search.

His body had floated 21 meters downstream from the rope swing, the inquest heard.

The 14-year-old was declared dead at the scene at around 6.30pm.

Detective Sergeant Danielle Grant told the inquest the pair had been the first to play on the rope swing.

She said: “Nobody else got around to having a try because it happened so quickly.”



Det Sgt Grant ordered the tree branch holding the swing to be cut down the following day.

Assistant Coroner Dunn told the court it was not the first tragedy he had investigated in the River Tyne.

He said: “I dealt with the inquest of Robert Hattersley, another young man killed in different circumstances in the same piece of river.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I remember sitting with his family and very much hoping I wouldn’t have to have another family, families, in front of me again.

“Here we are unfortunately with a similar set of circumstances.”

News.title: Shocking moment floor caves in at girls’ 15th birthday as panicked guests scream in terror and 11 rushed to hospital
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment the floor caved in at a girl’s 15th birthday party – leaving at least 11 injured.

Dozens of guests could be heard screaming in horror as the floor suddenly gave way at the bash in Brazil.





Partygoers plunge downwards, with at least 11 people injured as a result – some suffering broken bones and dislocations.

Just moments before the breakdown the birthday girl, Ana Beatriz, sat on a throne surrounded by hundreds of candles, as 230 guests watched on Sunday July 5, G1 reported.

People tumble into the basement, including the birthday girl, who was miraculously uninjured.

Marilia Ferreira, one of the injured guests, said: “It was a moment that will stay with me, I tried to sleep and it kept coming back to my mind.

“It was like a lid, then it collapsed and we fell down, a lot of people fell.

When I got up, my foot was bleeding a lot.”

When Ana’s mother saw the injured guests, she fainted in a state of shock.



The party, located in Belém, Brazil, took place in a historic mansion which is partly built on stilts towards its rear.

The site was closed after the collapse.

The family now demands the venue cover the costs of the botched party, which reportedly cost £5,800 (R$40,00), as well as providing support to the victims.

While the venue states they are cooperating with investigating authorities, the Civil Police say that the case was not registered.

Local City Hall is said to be monitoring the case and providing assistance to the victims while awaiting a technical assessment of the structure.



After two years of planning ended in disappointment, family and friends stepped in the very next day to stage an impromptu do-over for the 15-year-old.

The sweet moment was captured on video in which the group celebrate the honouree with cheers and applause as she walks down the street where her family live.

Even shaken attendees of the disaster party decided to gather to give the young birthday girl a proper party.

It comes after 150 people were evacuated from a Majorca hotel after the restaurant floor collapsed.

Two people were injured and taken to hospital.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Investigators suspect the 320-sq-ft dining room’s floor slabs caved in due to their age.

A full probe was launched to determine the cause of the collapse but cops think the flooring was not reinforced with wire mesh.

News.title: New hosepipe ban is announced for over a million Brits this week – check full list of 24 locations impacted
News.content:
A HOSEPIPE ban will come into effect for thousands of UK households later this week.

With temperatures set to hit 34C in some areas, restrictions will be in place to conserve water.





Southern Water will place a hosepipe ban on 24 towns across Hampshire and on the Isle of Wight.

Officially coming into force at a minute after midnight on Friday, July 10, the ban will help protect rivers in the area.

Under the restriction, hosepipes or sprinklers should not be used to water gardens, wash cars and patios, or fill swimming and paddling pools.

Southern Water explained that the ban has been brought in following “the warmest spring on record”.

The organisation revealed that the “record-breaking” heat has “left rivers 25 per cent lower than expected for this time of year”.

Hampshire’s River Test has lost a third of its water within the last month, according to Southern Water.

This has put the utility company under pressure to treat and supply water in the local area.

To protect local rivers, including the River Test and Itchen, and to “keep taps flowing”, Southern Water has implemented the latest ban.



The company acknowledged that customers with medical needs may still need to use a hosepipe, explaing that anyone on the Priority Services Register with medical or mobility needs are exempt.

Southern Water urged other households to do “anything you can do to reduce or avoid hosepipe use”.

It comes after another hosepipe ban was implemented across nine areas in Kent.

The restriction was brought in as a “very high level” of demand for drinking water was recorded.

South East Water said it was “deeply sorry for the disruption” which affected households in Sevenoaks, Tunbridge Wells, Snodland, Maidstone, Tenterden, Ashford, Faversham, Canterbury, and Herne Bay.

News.title: Prisoners now getting OZEMPIC and hair loss drugs shipped in by drone gangs, watchdog reveals
News.content:
INMATES in UK prisons are getting fat jabs and hair loss drugs shipped behind bars by drone gangs, a watchdog has revealed.

Chief Inspector of Prisons, Charlie Taylor, has told how drone gangs have made it possible for prisoners to pick from a “menu” of illicit substances banned in prisons.





Fat loss jab and hair loss drugs are reportedly on the list of smuggled contraband available to prisoners.

The banned substances are allegedly flown into prisons by gangs operating drones, some packages can weigh up to 4kg.

In an annual report Charlie Taylor said: “This just shows the scale of the problem the Prison Service is facing.

“Along with weight-loss drugs and others for hair loss, prisoners can buy anabolic steroids along with illegal drugs like cannabis and ketamine.



“Prisoners in some jails are able to pick off a menu, choosing from a range of different drugs.”

Taylor explained how prisoners serving lengthy sentences left with little to do all day will often turn to drugs to pass the time.



Gangs operating drones have “transformed” the drugs market behind bars, Taylor said.

As the tech becomes more advanced the size of illicit shipments has grown with inmates able to smuggle in larger and larger packages.

And, its not just drugs being smuggled into prisons, according to Taylor prisoners are able to bring in phones, memory sticks and chargers.

In his report, the Chief Inspector of Prisons reissued a previous warning that prisons have lost control of the airspace above jails.

Criminal organisations have exploited drone technology to seize control of the drugs trade behind bars.



Taylor’s report explains: “A failure across government to take this national security threat seriously means that many prisons are losing the fight against criminality.”

He added that senior figures in organised crime gangs are able to operate seemingly with impunity.

Taylor warned that crime bosses have managed to set up networks to make huge amounts of money by exploiting “drug-addicted and mentally ill prisoners.”



A previous Sun report showed gangs are raking in £50,000-a-time by flying drones packed with ­contraband into jails.

A £20 mobile can change hands for £2,000 in a prison, while a piece of paper soaked in Spice or cocaine fetches £1,000 a time.

A former lag who has spent almost 20 years at jails including Manchester and Hull, told us: “Some gangs are raking in £50,000 a go. If you put five phones on a drone and deliver them, that’s £10,000.

“Drugs change hands for huge amounts, and lots of sheets can be attached to a drone. Some prisoners are even ordering McDonald’s and KFC meals to show off.”

And, The Sun previously told how, in a bid to tackle the drone problem, HMP Woodhill became one of the first prisons in the country to get new heavy-duty steel grilles on cell windows.



Justice Secretary David Lammy has announced £35million worth of funding to fit the barriers on up to 13,000 windows at 17 high-risk prisons.

At Woodhill, the measures also include a cage made of metal mesh around the windows of a high-risk wing housing 60 dangerous criminals.

Drone sightings increased by 770 per cent between 2019 and 2023 and are now a common sight above jails including Woodhill.

And newer drones can be controlled from miles away, making it even harder to catch the operator.

Taylor’s report urged prisons to take action to tackle the drone issue, saying technology played an important role in disrupting contraband smuggling.



He said good use of body scanners, CCTV and drone countermeasures could help clamp down on the drone problem.

Taylor added, however, that: “Progress was undermined by a lack of other physical security measures, including gate security, windows and netting.”

His report concluded that the availability of illicit drugs was the most significant threat to safety in jails for adult men.

Taylor adds: “In our prisoner survey, 41 per cent of respondents told us it was easy to get drugs in their jail, and the figure remained stubbornly high at 57 per cent in category B training prisons.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prisons minister Lord Timpson said: “This report rightly highlights the serious challenges that remain in our prisons while noting encouraging signs of progress, with 76 per cent of recent inspections finding improvement, reflecting the dedication of prison staff working every day to turn lives around.



“There is much more to do, which is why we’ve also asked former Conservative home secretary Amber Rudd to lead an independent review that will help shape the next phase of reform – building on these green shoots to make our prisons safer and more secure, strengthen rehabilitation and better protect the public.”

News.title: Dentist murders sons, 7 & 12, firebombs his practice and kills himself in car fire after sending chilling warning to ex
News.content:
‘I’LL KILL EVERYONE’ Dentist murders sons, 7 & 12, firebombs his practice and kills himself in car fire after sending chilling warning to ex

A DENTIST murdered his two sons and firebombed his practice before killing himself in a car blaze – after threatening to “kill everyone” in an email to his children’s mother.

Mohammed Al-Lami, 40, is believed to have slaughtered his sons, aged 7 and 12, at his home in Ottawa, Canada.





The dentist was then discovered dead in burned-up car in Kemptville, said Ottawa Police.

Police also suspect Al-Lami set fire to the clinic where he worked in Iroquois.

The horrifying murders follow a slew of disturbing threats made two years earlier.

In a chilling email to his ex-wife in 2024, Al-Lami said: “I will kill everyone around you and your pimp… in a very wild and savage way.



“I won’t kill you. I will leave you alone, disabled in a wheelchair that you can’t move, even to visit your loved ones’ graves.

“I’ll make you an example of the unfair justice system. I will make you a worldwide story.”

Referring to his ex-wife’s partner, he added: “When you do something wrong to me, you pay for it. You pay for it either through the child support or whatever I feel suitable to respond to your actions until I end it the way I like for you and [your] pig.”

When officers stormed the dentist’s clinic on June 29 they found a sinister handwritten note from Al-Lami.



How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

The multi-page missive ranted against his ex-wife and family courts, claiming that she was the true abuser in the relationship.

Al-Lami had a turbulent history with his ex-wife – who he divorced in 2022.

Courts issued a probation order against him in 2024 because he threatened to hurt her.

The father then stopped sending child support – and sent his children’s mother horrifying threats of death and paralysing injury.



The mother did not believe her ex-husband would commit the crimes – but at the urging of her current partner and for the safety of her children she took the death taunts to authorities.

In court, she said: “I just felt, what if he literally, this happened? And then who’s going to be there for my kids if anything happened to me?”

Al-Lami told the judge he “didn’t have anything to say” to the horror allegations.

Police have launched an investigation into the suspected murder-suicide.

They urged the public: “Please check in on one another. If you or someone you know is struggling, consider reaching out to family, friends, a trusted community member, local support organizations, or professional services in your area. You do not have to navigate this alone.”

News.title: Missing girl, 4, presumed dead despite search as both parents face criminal charges
News.content:
Missing girl, 4, presumed dead despite search as both parents face criminal charges

A massive search and rescue operation was launched when Javeayah Harris, 4, was reported missing, with helicopters, drones, dogs and hundreds of police and volunteers combing more than 3,000 acres

View 4 Images Volunteers and police launched a massive search when Javeayah Harris was reported missing (Image: Jam Press)

A little girl at the centre of a huge missing persons search in South Carolina is now presumed dead after her parents were charged over her death.

Javeayah Harris, four, was reported missing, triggering a massive multi-agency search involving helicopters, drones, police dogs and hundreds of officers.

Aiken County cops have now said they believe the youngster had already died at least a month before she was first reported missing.

The police hunt for Javeayah has now switched from a frantic search operation to a homicide investigation, although her body has yet to be found.

View 4 Images Javeayah Harris is not presumed dead (Image: Jam Press)

Her father, Johmarea Harris, 23, has been charged with homicide by child abuse. Her mother, Michilae Herring, 22, has been charged with homicide by child abuse and filing a false police report.

The pair are both behind bars as police investigations into the whereabouts of their daughter’s body continue.

Authorities say evidence uncovered during the investigation led detectives to conclude Javeayah was already dead when the emergency call reporting her disappearance was made on June 30.

Aiken County Sheriff Marty Sawyer Jr. said: “Sadly, it was already too late to save her the moment the 911 call came in.”

View 4 Images Michilae Herring, 22, has been charged with homicide by child abuse and filing a false police report (Image: Jam Press)

Investigators are now continuing their search for the four-year-old’s remains outside Aiken County.

The initial search and rescue operation covered more than 3,000 acres using helicopters, drones, K-9 teams and hundreds of law enforcement personnel.

Now court documents show that both parents allegedly admitted the child had died, although police have not yet located her body. Investigators have said that further charges could follow as their investigation continues.

Meanwhile heartbroken locals have left a sea of flowers, teddy bears and balloons outside the family’s home as devastated residents pay tribute to the youngster.

View 4 Images Johmarea Harris, 23, has been charged with homicide by child abuse (Image: Jam Press)

Hundreds of volunteers from the local community joined in search efforts for the little girl after she was first reported missing. One local resident said: “She captured our hearts.”

Authorities previously described her as a bright and talkative little girl who loved Minnie Mouse and chasing chickens.

Sheriff Sawyer thanked the agencies and volunteers who assisted in the search and offered condolences to Javeayah’s extended family. Despite the grim developments, he vowed officers would continue searching until they find her.

Article continues below

He added: “Our search for Javeayah drives on. It is still extremely important that we bring her home.”

News.title: Toddler killer Jamie Varley's neighbour reported him to police years before tragic Preston Davey's murder
News.content:
Toddler killer Jamie Varley's neighbour reported him to police years before tragic Preston Davey's murder

A former neighbour has revealed the disturbing behaviour she says killer Jamie Varley displayed years before he murdered and sexually abused 13-month-old adopted toddler Preston Davey

View 3 Images Jamie Varley is serving a whole-life order for the horrific murder of Preston Davey (Image: Lancashire Police/PA Wire)

A former neighbour reported murderer Jamie Varley to the police after he threw lit cigarettes at her children’s toys in a bid to set them on fire.

‌



Varley, 37, is currently serving a rare whole-life order for the horrific murder and sexual abuse of his adopted 13-month-old son, Preston Davey, who was placed in the couple’s care in April 2023 at just nine months old before enduring horrific physical, sexual and emotional abuse at his hands.

‌



On the day of his tragic death, July 27, 2023, defenceless Preston suffered two sexual assaults at the hands of the former secondary school teacher. Varley’s former partner, John McGowan-Fazakerley, was jailed for 25 years for his role in the abuse and murder.

‌



View 3 Images Preston Davey was just 13-months old when he was murdered (Image: Lancashire Police/PA Wire)

Now, months after Varley’s sentencing, a former neighbour who lived next door to his family has spoken of the “nightmare” incidents she said she endured while living beside him.

The mother-of-five, who has fostered about a dozen children, said: “He [Varley] was horrible. I had to report him to the police and to the housing association for anti-social behaviour and criminal damage but he was never arrested.”

‌



She said his behaviour left her fearing for her children’s safety. She added: “He started shouting nasty abuse and ended up throwing lit cigarettes at their toys, trying to set them on fire.”

She told the Daily Mail: “I wouldn’t let my children play in the front of the house because of him, not unless I was on the doorstep. When his family moved out [in 2014], we put the flags out. How on earth he got to be a secondary school teacher, I really don’t know.”

The neighbour’s account is one of several troubling details to have emerged about Varley’s behaviour before Preston’s murder. During the Covid lockdown, Varley reportedly injured his back after falling from a ladder or drainpipe while allegedly spying on a boyfriend - not McGowan-Fazakerley - whom he suspected of being unfaithful.

‌



View 3 Images McGowan-Fazakerley was sentenced to 25 years in prison (Image: Lancashire Police/PA Wire)

Following his sentencing at Preston Crown Court last month, Varley joined the grim roll call of Britain’s most dangerous offenders condemned to die in prison. He joins offenders including Wayne Couzens, Levi Bellfield and Jeremy Bamber.

Preston was born to convicted murderer Sarah Davey on June 16, 2022. Just five days later, the 5lb 7oz baby was taken into the care of Oldham Council. Varley and McGowan-Fazakerley were approved as adoptive parents in January 2023 before Preston moved into their Blackpool home in April that year.

Article continues below

Over the following months, Preston suffered escalating physical, sexual and emotional abuse at the hands of Varley, while McGowan-Fazakerley turned a blind eye. On July 23, 2023, the pair carried out a joint attack on the toddler as he slumped helplessly over the bars of his cot.

Four days later, on July 27, Preston was rushed to Blackpool Victoria Hospital in cardiac arrest. Despite the efforts of medics, he was pronounced dead at 7.18pm.

News.title: NHS major update as children born after December 2019 can get jab
News.content:
NHS major update as children born after December 2019 can get jab

Parents are being told to 'book now' in certain circumstances

View 2 Images A reminder has been issued to parents (Image: Getty Images)

Parents are being reminded to check their child's vaccination record after the NHS issued a fresh update about protection against four infectious diseases. If your child was born after a certain date and has missed a dose, they could now be eligible for an alternative vaccine.

‌



In a post shared on X, the NHS urged parents whose children have missed one or both doses of their MMR or MMRV vaccine to book an appointment with their GP practice if they receive an invitation. The reminder comes as the health service continues efforts to improve childhood vaccination uptake.

‌



The MMRV vaccine protects against measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. It is being offered to eligible children born on or after December 1, 2019, who are invited by their GP practice after missing one or both routine vaccinations.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Previously, children routinely received separate MMR and chickenpox vaccines where eligible. The introduction of the combined MMRV vaccine means eligible children can receive protection against all four illnesses in a single injection, reducing the number of appointments and injections needed.

The NHS says the MMRV vaccine is offered as part of a phased rollout in England and is available only to children born on or after December 1, 2019. Parents whose children are eligible will be contacted by their GP practice when it is time to book an appointment.

‌



It comes amid continued concern over falling uptake of childhood vaccinations. According to the UK Health Security Agency, measles cases have increased in England in recent years, with health officials warning that lower vaccination rates have allowed the virus to spread more easily.

View 2 Images Measles is on the up in the UK (Image: Getty Images)

UKHSA figures show there were over 800 cases of measles in the first half of 2026 and 2 reported deaths, compared to 959 cases for the whole of 2025. There have been clusters of measles cases reported in areas of the country, with every region of England seeing cases.

‌



Figures also show a gap of 7.5% in vaccine coverage between the least and the most deprived areas of the country. The vaccination rate for both MMR doses at age five years in England is 84.1% (Jan – March 2026), lower than the 95% target set by the World Health Organization (WHO) and in January this year the WHO confirmed that the UK had lost its measles elimination status.

The NHS says two doses of the MMR vaccine provide the best protection against measles, mumps and rubella. Vaccination is the most effective way of preventing serious complications, including meningitis, hearing loss and, in rare cases, inflammation of the brain.

Chickenpox is usually a mild illness, but it can sometimes lead to complications including skin infections, pneumonia and inflammation of the brain, particularly in babies, adults and people with weakened immune systems. The combined MMRV vaccine helps protect against these risks while reducing the number of injections children need.

Article continues below

Parents who think their child has missed one or both doses do not need to start the vaccination schedule again. Instead, the NHS advises contacting your GP practice to arrange any outstanding vaccinations and discussing whether your child is eligible for the combined MMRV vaccine if they have been invited.

News.title: Boss slammed for letting England fans have lie in to 11am on Monday
News.content:
Boss slammed for letting England fans have lie in to 11am on Monday

The CEO has been criticised for her policy

Boss slammed for letting England fans have lie in to 11am on Monday

A boss who let staff have a lie-in after England’s World Cup clash has found herself at the centre of a furious online row. Charly Gillespie-Smith offered employees a later start after the Three Lions v Mexico match if they could prove they had watched it.

‌



While some hailed the move as a brilliant workplace perk, others accused the London CEO of attention-seeking and branded the policy “rage bait”. The founder of social media agency Lasting Lemons told staff they could arrive at 11am instead of 9:30am if they submitted photographic evidence showing they had tuned in to watch England.

‌



The offer quickly went viral online, sparking a flood of criticism from disgruntled social media users. One person said: “Got to be rage bait.”

‌



View 3 Images Charly's email to her employees

Another critic added: “Virtue signalling at its best.” Someone else commented: “What a strange email.” A fourth person wrote: “This should definitely be rage bait.”

‌



One other person posted: “Do employees have to show pictures of their vomit if they’re sick?” But Charly defended the decision, insisting it helped create a positive workplace culture.

“I think giving people the chance to enjoy special moments, even when work is busy, helps build a positive environment," she said. “We’re a social media agency – we work very hard and often across odd hours, so I try to be flexible when big events like the World Cup come around.

“It’s easier to do that when you have a dedicated team. We have a WhatsApp group, and people sent messages like ‘best boss EVER’.”

‌



View 3 Images Charly with employee Eddy Wynne watching the match

The email was sent to staff on 2 July ahead of England’s match, with workers able to take advantage of the later start if they provided proof they had been watching. Charly said the policy reflected the company’s approach to flexibility and work-life balance.

‌



She said: “There are 10 of us on the team, and everyone made different choices. Some were big England fans and went out to watch the game, some watched from bed, and others chose to get a good night’s sleep instead.”

As criticism mounted online, members of the Lasting Lemons team rallied to defend their boss. In a video posted on the agency’s TikTok account, one employee said: “Our boss is being cancelled for letting us watch the England game. Surely not?”

View 3 Images Lasting Lemons employees during the match

Article continues below

Many others backed the idea and said more employers should take a similar approach. One supporter wrote: “This is how every company should be.”

Another fan said: “Now that’s what you call a good good company to work for.”

News.title: Pharmacist settles debate on whether paracetamol or ibuprofen is better
News.content:
Pharmacist settles debate on whether paracetamol or ibuprofen is better

A pharmacist has shared his advice on which painkiller to take

View 2 Images Which you should take may depend (Image: Grace Cary via Getty Images)

When you find yourself feeling unwell, or experiencing aches or pains, you might reach for some common painkillers - such as ibuprofen or paracetamol. But which you should take depends on a few things.

‌



Thankfully an expert has spoken exclusively to the Mirror about painkillers - and settled the debate once and for all on which is best to take. Abbas Kanani, superintendent pharmacist at Chemist Click, previously explained which is more beneficial when it comes to paracetamol or ibuprofen, and debunked a common misconception many people hold about them. He said: "Paracetamol is probably more effective at bringing down temperature, so it's almost like a double-whammy, you get rid of your headache and bring your temperature down.

‌



"But if you feel that you have more body aches, that's your main symptom, then ibuprofen is probably slightly better as it's an anti-inflammatory." The expert also warned that people should be cautious when taking ibuprofen, as many are allergic to the class of drug it belongs to. You can find out more about who shouldn't take ibuprofen and other NSAIDs here

‌



However, he reveals that what most people don't realise is that you can actually take both medicines together when you're feeling particularly under the weather. "If you feel that one isn't enough you can take ibuprofen as well as paracetamol, you can take them together. A lot of people don't know that it's not one or the other, you can put them together as they work in different ways."

View 2 Images The pharmacist has given his expert insight on the best painkillers (Image: Abbas Kanani)

Article continues below

While paracetamol and ibuprofen can ease aches, pains and high temperatures, as well as mild cold and flu symptoms, Abbas notes they offer little relief for those struggling with coughs and nasal congestion.

To tackle these particular symptoms, cold and flu remedies would be more appropriate. For example, a decongestant-based medicine would be most effective for a blocked nose, while an expectorant would be needed for a chesty cough and a cough suppressant for a dry, tickly cough.

However, when using cold and flu medicines, always check the packaging and leaflet to confirm which other products can be safely combined, as while paracetamol and ibuprofen can be taken together, they may not be compatible with other medications.

News.title: Boy, 13, tried to save friend, 14, before pair both died in River Tyne tragedy
News.content:
Boy, 13, tried to save friend, 14, before pair both died in River Tyne tragedy

David Ionut Radut, 14, fell from a rope swing by the River Tyne in Ovingham, Northumberland, and Aras Rudzianskas, 13, went into the water to help him, an inquest heard

View 5 Images David Ionut Radut, 14, and Aras Rudzianskas, 13, drowned

Two teenagers drowned in a river after one went into the water to help the other who had fallen from a rope swing and could not swim, an inquest heard.

‌



David Ionut Radut, 14, and Aras Rudzianskas, 13, had been playing by the River Tyne in Ovingham, Northumberland, when the tragedy happened.

‌



Northumberland Coroner's Court heard how David, who could not swim, let go of the swing too early and landed in a deeper part of the river. He got into difficulty in the water, shouted for help and Aras ran into the water to try and save him.

‌



David pushed Aras under the water in his panic and they both struggled, the inquest was told. Another child, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, tried to help David by grabbing his arms, but had to let go as they could feel themselves getting into difficulty and swam back to the river bank.

View 5 Images Aras went into the water to help his friend (Image: Family Handout/PA)

Huge blaze near Turnpike Lane Tube Station as 80 firefighters race to scene READ MORE :

Assistant Coroner Paul Dunn said something grabbed their leg and they were unsure if it was the current or David, reported ChronicleLive.

‌



David went under the water and was not seen again and Aras, who was face down in the water with his arms spread, was taken by the current. Fiona Matthews, who was paddleboarding in the river, found Aras face down in the water.

The Coroner's Court, sitting at County Hall in Morpeth, heard how Fiona came across something which looked like a pale rock and discovered it was Aras' back. She turned him over, pulled him onto her paddleboard and began giving him chest compressions.

View 5 Images David Radut fell into the water from a rope swing, an inquest heard (Image: Family Handout/PA)

‌



She said: "I pulled him under the arms and used his shorts to try and get him out of the water. I think the adrenaline kicked in."

Fiona told the hearing how she tried to continue giving chest compressions while paddling towards the river bank. She said: "I had lost my paddle by then so I was using my hands to paddle."

Fiona said she had decided to kneel rather than stand up on her paddleboard that day due to the water not being as flat as it previously was. She managed to get Aras closer to the river bank and paramedics took over in the water.

‌



Paramedics managed to get Aras' heart beating again but he was unable to breath on his own. He was rushed to the Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI) in Newcastle by air ambulance where he died three days later.

View 5 Images Aras' family placed a plaque in his memory in Ovingham (Image: Simon Greener/Newcastle Chronicle)

Police officers from the marine unit continued to search the river for David. His body was found on the bed of the river at 6.30pm that evening and he was taken by ambulance to the RVI.

‌



Detective Sergeant Danielle Grant, of Northumbria Police, requested for the tree branch, which contained the swing, to be cut down the next morning. She told the court: "I was informed an unknown person has gone down and cut down the entire tree."

The court heard how David and Aras, who both lived in Newcastle, were part of a group of around 20 children who travelled to Ovingham from the city on May 18, 2024. They had been at the river less than half an hour when the incident happened.

The pair were the first to take turns to use the swing, which was attached to a tree branch, to swing out over the river and back again. DS Grant said: "Nobody else had got around to having a try because it happened so quickly."

‌



View 5 Images Aras' mum Eagle Rudzianskiene with the plaque (Image: Simon Greener/Newcastle Chronicle)

When they got into difficulty in the water, some of the children flagged down a bus for help. Northumbria Police received three phone calls about the incident in quick succession.

Ben Corlett, who was in the area at the time, told the inquest: "There was a lot of panic, a lot of hysteria, crying and shouting. I didn't realise what happened at first. When I saw them run out in front of the bus I thought maybe one of them had been hit."

‌



The first call to police, at 3.29pm, stated that two mates had jumped into Ovingham river and were dead. No further details could be obtained as the caller was so distraught.

Two minutes later, a passenger on the bus which had been flagged down by children, reported that someone had drowned. At 3.35pm, a third caller said that two males had drowned. They said one male had been struggling in the water, causing another to help, they had been pulled under.

David's family asked why they were not notified about the incident until 6.50pm. PC Grant told them that police initially did not know which male was which as the descriptions given of them were similar and they had no belongings on them.

‌



Coroner Dunn told the hearing how he was dealing with the inquests as he had previously been the coroner during the inquest of Robert Hattersley, 13, who also drowned in the River Tyne near Ovingham in 2022.

He told the court: "I dealt with the inquest of Robert Hattersley, another young man killed in different circumstances in the same piece of river. I remember sitting with his family and very much hoping I wouldn't have to have another family, families, in front of me again and here are unfortunately with a similar set of circumstances."

The inquest continues.

Article continues below

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: 'I saved £1,280 by taking kids out of school for a holiday even with the fine'
News.content:
'I saved £1,280 by taking kids out of school for a holiday even with the fine'

A British mum took her kids out of school for a family holiday ended up receiving a £160 fine - but says the overall saving on the trip meant it was worth it

View 3 Images Thea received a fine for taking her 5-year-old out of school (Image: Jam Press/@thearule)

A mum slapped with a £160 fine for taking her son out of school for a family holiday says she has no regrets because ultimately she saved £1,280 on her trip.

‌



Thea Rule decided to take her son Roman, five, out of school to jet off for a week in Majorca, after her request for authorised absence was refused by the school.

‌



"I don’t care what anyone says, he’s in reception class and we’re getting on that plane,” Thea told NeedToKnow. “I believe that my child should be able to enjoy family time with us. I asked via a handwritten letter but was refused. He is in reception class and we did not think it would impact his learning."

‌



Thea claims the same holiday during the school holidays would have cost an eye-watering £1,440 more because of soaring travel prices. The school issued her with a £160 fine, but the family still saved £1,280 overall by travelling during term time.

View 3 Images Thea says she had lots of support from other parents online (Image: Jam Press/@thearule)

Foreign Office updates Italy travel advice with stark warning for Brits this summer READ MORE :

She said: "I would never consider taking Roman away during term time if he was doing his SATS or GCSEs. But a week off at the age of five…we as his parents did not believe it would hinder his education. He experienced culture, social interactions and learned other bits along the way.

‌



"Roman was able to learn about the old town of Alcudia, go swimming and snorkelling with sea wildlife and enjoy time with us and his younger brother, all things I believe to be fantastic experiences. Roman is successful at school and is on course to meet his learning outcomes before the end of the year."

Thea said the huge difference in holiday prices was the main reason behind the decision, and claimed that after she shared her story online, dozens of parents backed her stance.

After sharing her story online, she claimed that dozens of parents backed her stance.

‌



View 3 Images The family saved over £1,200 taking their kids on holiday outside of the school holidays (Image: Jam Press/@thearule)

World's most overcrowded holiday spot with over 100 tourists to every local READ MORE :

Thea said: "They all agreed reception is not a school year that requires as much attendance as other years. I thanked them for understanding and I know others do the same. We were honest and requested the holiday but others I know say their children are sick and therefore don’t get fined for taking their children out."

The mother-of-two has encouraged other parents to book holidays strategically if they are looking to save money, adding that she believes the memories made with family outweighed the worrying about fines.

‌



While for Thea and her family there was a saving to be had, there's one little-known rule around term-time fines that families should be aware of. A lot of parents don't realise that the fine isn't applied per family, but per parent per child.

Fines also need to be paid as soon as they are issued. In England, the initial fine per person is £80 if paid within 21 days, but jumps to £160 if paid within 28 days.

But with the per parent/child rule, that means if two adults go away with two children, you could instantly be facing a cost of up to £320. Meanwhile, a second offence could see you hit with a higher £160 fine, so for a family of four that could be £640 total; depending on your choice of holiday and timing, that may negate the savings potentially gained from travelling inside school holidays.

Article continues below

Still, it's no surprise that parents like Thea are still choosing to take kids out of school and face the fines instead. Travel prices notoriously hike up during the school holidays, sometimes even tripling including UK holiday parks.

Do you think parents should be fined for taking their kids out of school for holidays? Email us at webtravel@reachplc.com

News.title: Huge 7,500-tonne illegal rubbish dump found next to ex-Premier League ground after locals' sniff foul stench
News.content:
Huge 7,500-tonne illegal rubbish dump found next to ex-Premier League ground after locals' sniff foul stench

Residents were forced to shut their windows during the heatwave after a foul stench led to the discovery of a 7,500-tonne illegal waste dump outside Bradford City's stadium

View 3 Images The waste dump stretched across a 50-metre site opposite Bradford City's stadium (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

A 7,500-tonne illegal waste dump has been discovered opposite a football stadium.

‌



Drone footage showed mountains of household and commercial rubbish piled across a strip of land just yards from Valley Parade in Bradford, West Yorks. The waste stretched for around half the length of a football pitch, with hundreds of black bin bags, towering piles of rubbish and rusting containers scattered across the site in Manningham. The back end of an articulated lorry could also be seen.

‌



The sprawling dump stretched across a 50-metre (164ft) long strip opposite the home of League One side Bradford City FC. Residents raised the alarm during the recent heatwave after a “rotten” smell spread across the area, forcing some to keep their windows and doors shut. The Environment Agency (EA) has now launched an investigation and said officers were working to identify those responsible.

‌



View 3 Images The site sat opposite Bradford City's stadium (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

One resident, who wished to remain anonymous, said locals had noticed “strange” trucks entering the site in the early mornings and evenings. They said: “This issue came to light when we had the recent heatwave and the local area was overcome by a disgusting smell of rotten foods and waste.

“We were not able to leave windows or doors open due to the disgusting and pungent smell. It was only after many of the local residents were discussing this issue it was highlighted that many of them had seen trucks entering a parcel of land on Midland Road that has been locked for many years during the early mornings and evening which I felt was very strange.”

‌



The resident said they later looked over the wall surrounding the site and spotted an excavator moving large bags of waste.

They said: “I walk daily along this road so decided to try and look over the wall to see what was being done on the land as there were no signs for any business at the gate. I was able to catch a glimpse as it’s a big wall with a huge drop and vegetation on the other side and saw a excavator moving around huge black bags of waste.

“There was an artic (articulated) trailer as well as some sort of incinerator. That same evening I saw a removal truck outside the premises waiting to access the property. It was also being discussed on a local community group and pictures and videos were taken - these were uploaded to the group and the excavator was removed from the site.”

‌



View 3 Images The Environment Agency launched an investigation after receiving reports about the site (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

In a joint statement, Manningham’s Independent councillors said they were “deeply appalled”. They said: “This is completely unacceptable and represents a blatant disregard for our community and the environment. We will not tolerate anyone treating our community as a dumping ground.

“Illegal waste dumping, in any form or on any scale, has no place in Manningham. We are aware of the ongoing investigation and sincerely hope those responsible are identified, prosecuted where appropriate, and held fully accountable for their actions.”

‌



The councillors said they “immediately referred” the matter to the Environment Agency after residents raised concerns last week. They added early reports suggested HGVs travelled into Manningham from outside the area to dump the waste. If confirmed, they said the operation appeared to be “organised”, making it “even more disgraceful”.

An Environment Agency spokesperson confirmed officers received reports on Wednesday, July 1. The spokesperson confirmed reports was received on July 1. They said: "Officers attended and estimated multiple tonnes of mixed household and commercial waste has been dumped. They are following up several lines of enquiry to track down those responsible, and working to trace the landowner to ensure the site is properly secured.

"They’re also working with partners at Bradford Council, West Yorkshire Police and West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service. The Environment Agency is also appealing for information from the public.”

Article continues below

Ben Hocking, area environment manager at the Environment Agency, said: “We have launched an investigation to find those responsible for illegal waste dumping in central Bradford so they can be held to account. We are assessing the site’s environmental impact and making enquiries to trace the landowner to ensure the site is secured.

“Waste crime scars communities and under our 10 Point Plan we’re acting quickly to tackle illegal activity and shut down sites.”

Cllr Ian Walker, Bradford Council’s executive member for neighbourhoods and communities, said the council was aware of the site and confirmed the Environment Agency was leading the investigation, which it would “support”.

News.title: Belgium say 'sense of injustice' spurred them on to knock US out of World Cup
News.content:
Belgium midfielder Nicolas Raskin said his team felt a "sense of injustice" over United States striker Folarin Balogun's one-match ban being suspended by Fifa shortly before their World Cup last-16 match.

Balogun, 25, appeared certain to miss the tie in Seattle after being shown a straight red card for a foul on Bosnia-Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic in the previous round.

But on Sunday Fifa suspended the automatic one-match ban for 12 months, leading to widespread criticism, with Uefa, Belgium and England boss Thomas Tuchel among those speaking out against the ruling.

On Monday US President Donald Trump said he asked Fifa to review Balogun's ban, which he said would have left a "big stain" on the tournament.

But, despite the American star striker being cleared to play and starting the match, Belgium convincingly beat the tournament co-hosts 4-1.

"A lot has happened off the pitch over the last two days,"said Belgium and Rangers midfielder Raskin.

"There was a sense of injustice within the squad, and we were determined to respond on the field."

Belgium captain Youri Tielemans insisted the affair had boosted his side.

"We told ourselves we had to respond on the pitch. That's what we did," he said.

After Belgium scored their fourth goal several of their players were pictured dancing in a style similar to the 'Trump dance' - where he rocks his hips and slowly pumps his arms - which gained notoriety during the 2024 US presidential campaign.

The official Instagram account for the Belgium national team also appeared to mock the debacle, posting a picture of striker Romelu Lukaku cupping his ear with the caption "overturn this".

News.title: One million more UK homeowners set  to face higher mortgages
News.content:
The impact of the Iran war means a million more homeowners face higher mortgage bills than the Bank of England had previously expected.

Just over five million homeowners should expect their monthly mortgage repayments to increase by the end of 2028, according to Bank forecasts.

That compared to four million projected by the Bank in December.

However, the Bank's Financial Stability Report said the hit would not be as hard as seen in recent years.

A typical owner-occupier rolling off a fixed rate in the next two years is likely to face an increase of Â£45 on their monthly mortgage bill, the Bank said. That compares to a typical rise of Â£120 for those getting a new deal between the end of 2022 and end of 2024.

However, 750,000 homeowners who are paying less than 3% interest on their current deal would be rolling off these products this year and would see an average increase of Â£170 per month in repayments, the Bank said.

More than eight in 10 mortgage customers have fixed-rate deals.

The interest rate on this kind of mortgage does not change until the deal expires, usually after two or five years, and a new one is chosen to replace it.

More than two million borrowers on a two-year fixed deal expiring by the end of 2028 were projected to remortgage close to their existing rate and see little change in repayments, the Bank said.

However, these borrowers were now unlikely to see repayments fall over coming years, as had been forecast prior to the Iran conflict.

News.title: MI5 knew agent was misogynist 'obsessed' with violence, watchdog finds
News.content:
A secret inquiry by MI5's watchdog concluded the security service knew an abusive agent it defended in court was a misogynist who was "obsessed" with violence, the BBC can reveal.

The inquiry took place after BBC News originally exposed how MI5 had covered up for the man - a neo-Nazi informant known publicly as agent X.

The government took the BBC to court in 2022 in a failed attempt to block our investigation, but it won agent X legal anonymity.

That year, the BBC first reported how the MI5 spy had used his status to coercively control his girlfriend, including attacking her with a machete, before moving abroad to continue intelligence work while he was still under investigation.

Following the BBC story, the office of the investigatory powers commissioner (IPCO) Sir Brian Leveson launched an inquiry, which - like much of IPCO's work - was secret. Details of the inquiry can now be reported for the first time.

In response to the new revelations, the spy's former partner, known as Beth, told the BBC: "I'd like to see a full apology for the fact that MI5 actually were willing to use somebody like X and the fact they were aware of his abuse towards me and they did nothing at all."

News.title: Endometriosis diagnosis set to be sped up with two new tests carried out by GPs
News.content:
People who think they may have endometriosis - a painful condition affecting one in 10 women - will soon be able to ask their GP for a couple of non-invasive tests for quicker diagnosis.

Experts hope they will be a game-changer and cut the nine-year or longer waits patients can currently face.

One is a spit test that looks for genetic material. The other measures electrical signals in the gut using sensor pads on the abdomen.

Both are being recommended under new draft guidance, external for the NHS in England and Wales, alongside regular checks, to help identify the condition where cells similar to those in the lining of the womb grow elsewhere in the body.
